test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: By which year does the National Education Policy 2020 aim for a 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in school education?
solution:
The correct answer is **__2030__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• By 2030, the 100% **Gross Enrollment Ratio** in School Education is the goal set forth in **National Education Policy 2020**.
 
• Through the open schooling system, **NEP 2020** will reintegrate 2 crore out-of-school youngsters.
 
• The NCTE will cooperate with **NCERT** to develop a brand-new, comprehensive **National Curriculum Framework for Teacher Education, **or **NCFTE** 2021. By 2030, a 4-year integrated B.Ed degree will be the prerequisite for teaching.
 
• The policy places a strong emphasis on the necessity of ensuring that every child enrolled in school is able to finish their education and meet learning objectives.
 
• Mother tongue or regional language should be used for instruction up to at least Grade 5. No pupil will be forced to learn a language.
 
• Assessment changes that assess student progress toward reaching learning outcomes using a **360-degree holistic progress card**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Together, the Center and the States will expand public investment in the education sector to, at the earliest, 6% of **GDP**.
 
• In order to offer a forum for the open exchange of thoughts on the use of technology to improve learning, evaluation, planning, and administration, the **National Educational Technology Forum (NETF) **will be established.
 
• In 15 years, college affiliation will be phased down, and a framework will be set up to provide institutions varying degrees of autonomy. Every college is expected to eventually become either an autonomous college that awards degrees or a constituent college of a university.
 
• A single, comprehensive umbrella organisation for all higher education, except medical and legal education, would be established as the** Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)**. The **National Higher Education Regulatory Council (NHERC)** will be responsible for regulation, the **General Education Council (GEC) **will define standards, the **Higher Education Grants Council (HEGC) **will provide money, and the **National Accreditation Council (NAC)** will oversee accreditation. Universities that are both public and private will be subject to the same regulations, accreditation requirements, and academic standards.
 
• By 2035, the gross enrollment ratio in higher education is expected to increase to 50%, and 3.5 crore seats would be added.
 
• In both urban and rural India, basic and higher education are covered under the national policy on education.
 
 
• The **Education Commission'**s recommendations served as the foundation for the first **NPE **(1964-66). This programme aimed to achieve national cohesion and greater economic and cultural development by "radical revamping" India's educational system and equating chances for education for everyone.
 
• The NPE also demanded that all children receive the obligatory education that is spelled forth in the Indian **Constitution **up until the age of fourteen.
 
• The first education policy for the twenty-first century in India is NEP 2020. The National Education Policy 2020 places a strong emphasis on the development of each student's creative potential.
 
• Ancient academics including** Charaka and Susruta, Aryabhata, Bhaskaracharya, Chanakya, Madhava, Patanjali, Panini, **and **Thiruvalluvar** were referenced in the NEP 2020.
 
 
 
• The National Education Commission, also known as** Rashtriya Shiksha Aayog**, was suggested by the NEP as the country's top educational authority.
